summary: Append six distinct itemized U.S. military aircraft loss/damage classes from the September Lead Inspector General synthesis and May CENTCOM admission: 4 AH-6 deliberately destroyed, 1 A-10 destroyed, 1 AH-64 shot down, 1 F-35A damaged, 1 HH-60W damaged, 1 MQ-1 shot down. Preserve imprecise event dates and all 41 prior accepted packets.

sources.source_role: Official September 2026 Lead Inspector General report to Congress, Table 5 on printed page 18 (PDF page index 19): detailed aircraft loss/damage disposition; source table derives from May CRS and Aug24 CENTCOM vetting
sources.outlet: U.S. Department of Defense Lead Inspector General / USAID OIG hosted
sources.title: Operation Epic Fury, Report to Congress, April 1-June 30, 2026

sources.source_role: CENTCOM May 31 original statement confirms Iran shot down a U.S. MQ-1 operating over international waters; no exact event timestamp given
sources.title: U.S. Defends, Disables Threats in Response to Iranian Aggression

record.disposition: Four unrecoverable AH-6 helicopters deliberately destroyed by U.S. forces during combat search and rescue; not four enemy shootdowns
record.note: Lead IG Table 5 lists four AH-6 destroyed by U.S. forces after deemed unrecoverable in CSAR. Specific individual tail numbers and destruction day(s) are not in this source. Do not combine with MC-130J self-destruction, non-AH6 helicopters, or Iranian kinetic BDA.

record.disposition: One A-10 destroyed after damage during return from CSAR mission
record.note: Lead IG Table 5: one A-10 destroyed, jettisoned due to damage on return from CSAR. Specific adversary causing prior damage not identified by this cited table; do not tag as a confirmed Iranian shootdown. Distinct from later damaged A-10 cited by October CRS.

record.disposition: One AH-64 shot down over Strait of Hormuz; specific date, perpetrator and recovery status not in Lead IG Table 5
record.note: The September Lead IG Table 5 confirms one AH-64 shot down over SoH but does not provide date or detailed shooter attribution. Preserve lost status rather than claiming independently surveyed wreckage/destruction. Do not conflate with AH-6 rescue aircraft.

record.disposition: One F-35A damaged by enemy fire over Iran, not destroyed or shot down
record.note: Lead IG Table 5 says one F-35A damaged due to enemy fire over Iran. Recovery/return-to-service status not in cited table. Do not turn the airframe into a destroyed F-35 in the Lie Ledger or blend it with the April F-15E losses.

record.item: HH-60W Jolly Green II search-and-rescue helicopter
record.disposition: One HH-60W damaged during CSAR operation; no confirmed destroyed airframe
record.note: Lead IG Table 5 corroborates one HH-60W damaged during aircrew rescue. Damage cause, repair and serial not specified by table. Do not count as an Iranian direct shootdown.

record.disposition: One U.S. MQ-1 shot down by Iranian forces while operating over waters described by CENTCOM as international
record.note: CENTCOM May 31 confirms U.S. MQ-1 downed by Iran, but does not provide exact crash time or airframe serial. The 2026-05-31 suffix denotes U.S. announcement date, not a verified incident minute. Iran separately claims territorial waters, so exact sea jurisdiction is DISPUTED. This is ONE of CRS's three MQ-1 reported losses as of Oct5, not a fourth MQ-1 or an MQ-9.
